summary: [¶] - (a) On 12.01.2024, the Petitioner applied for the grant of connectivity for a 400 MW solar project under the LAND BG route at the Pachora PS in Madhya Pradesh. Petitioner also furnished a bank guarantee in lieu of Land dated 12.01.2024, amounting to Rs. 40 Crore. CTUIL granted in-principle connectivity to the Petitioner on 10.04.2024. Thereafter, Petitioner submitted Conn-BG1, Conn-BG2, and Conn-BG3 on 09.05.2024. Accordingly, under Regulation 9 of the GNA Regulations, CTUIL was obligated to issue final connectivity to the Petitioner by 14.05.2024, i.e., 15 days from the date of submission of the bank guarantee by the Petitioner. However, CTUIL has not to date issued final connectivity to the Petitioner. [¶] - (h) Commission on 09.09.2025 issued the Third Amendment, whereby _inter alia_ Regulation 9.3 was inserted to permit a change in the source of connectivity even prior to the grant of final connectivity. Petitioner, vide its email dated 15.09.2025, issued a letter requesting CTUIL to issue a final grant of connectivity to the Petitioner, permit the Petitioner to change the source of connectivity under the Third Amendment, [¶] revocation of the in-principle connectivity granted to the Petitioner for a limited period till the Petitioner’s application is taken up for hearing and considered by this Commission. Accordingly, the present IA 129/2025 has been filed. He also apprised the Commission that the Petitioner’s grievance is squarely covered now by the order dated 8.12.2025 in Petition No. 14/SM/2025, whereby the Commission has exercised its power to remove difficulties for effective implementation of the Third Amendment to the GNA Regulations, 2022, and, according to the Petitioner, nothing survives in the matter. In the alternative, the learned senior counsel pressed for interim relief, including a stay on the revocation of the in-principle grant of connectivity to the Petitioner. [para 19] 19. CTUIL submitted that vide letter dated 10.04.2024, in-principle grant of connectivity for 400 MW (Solar Project) at Pachora Pooling Station was issued to the Petitioner under augmentation without ATS. The augmentation elements required for the grant of connectivity included Rajgarh Phase-I, Phase-II and PhaseIII, and the implementation of certain elements depended on the award and commissioning of the identified transmission system. As per the GNA Regulations prevailing prior to the Third Amendment, a final grant of connectivity could be issued only after the firm start date of connectivity was ascertained; hence, CTUIL could not issue a final grant of Connectivity to the Petitioner. CTUIL submitted that, as per Regulation 11A(1) of the GNA Regulations, the Petitioner was required to submit documents towards ownership or lease rights or land use rights within 18 months of the in-principle grant of connectivity or 12 months of the final grant, whichever is earlier. Accordingly, the due date for submission of land documents was 10.10.2025. However, the Petitioner failed to submit the required land documents under Regulation 11A (1). Since the Petitioner did not comply with Regulation 11A(1) by the due date, CTUIL revoked the in-principle connectivity vide letter dated 04.12.2025.
